name: fragrance
note: Umbrella term covering many compounds; the most common cause of cosmetic allergic contact dermatitis.

name: limonene
note: Citrus fragrance component; allergenic especially when oxidized. One of the 26 EU-labeled fragrance allergens.

name: linalool
note: Floral fragrance component; allergenic when oxidized. One of the 26 EU-labeled fragrance allergens.

name: citral
note: Lemon-scented fragrance component; EU-labeled fragrance allergen.

name: geraniol
note: Rose-scented fragrance component; EU-labeled fragrance allergen.

name: citronellol
note: Fragrance component; EU-labeled fragrance allergen.

name: eugenol
note: Clove-scented fragrance component; EU-labeled fragrance allergen.

name: isoeugenol
note: Fragrance component; EU-labeled fragrance allergen.

name: coumarin
note: Sweet hay-scented fragrance component; EU-labeled fragrance allergen.

name: cinnamal
note: Cinnamon-scented fragrance component; EU-labeled fragrance allergen.

name: cinnamyl alcohol
note: Fragrance component; EU-labeled fragrance allergen.

name: benzyl alcohol
note: Fragrance component and preservative; EU-labeled fragrance allergen.

name: benzyl benzoate
note: Fragrance component; EU-labeled fragrance allergen.

name: benzyl salicylate
note: Fragrance component; EU-labeled fragrance allergen.

name: hexyl cinnamal
note: Fragrance component; EU-labeled fragrance allergen.

name: hydroxycitronellal
note: Fragrance component; EU-labeled fragrance allergen.

name: alpha-isomethyl ionone
note: Fragrance component; EU-labeled fragrance allergen.

name: farnesol
note: Fragrance component; EU-labeled fragrance allergen.

name: myroxylon pereirae resin
note: Natural resin and classic patch-test allergen; cross-reacts with many fragrances and flavorings.

name: methylisothiazolinone
note: Preservative; among the most common causes of cosmetic contact dermatitis in recent years.

name: methylchloroisothiazolinone
note: Preservative usually paired with methylisothiazolinone; a frequent contact allergen.

name: formaldehyde
note: Preservative and well-known contact allergen.

name: quaternium-15
note: Formaldehyde-releasing preservative; common contact allergen.

name: dmdm hydantoin
note: Formaldehyde-releasing preservative; can trigger formaldehyde-sensitive skin.

name: imidazolidinyl urea
note: Formaldehyde-releasing preservative; can trigger formaldehyde-sensitive skin.

name: diazolidinyl urea
note: Formaldehyde-releasing preservative; can trigger formaldehyde-sensitive skin.

name: 2-bromo-2-nitropropane-1,3-diol
note: Formaldehyde-releasing preservative (bronopol); recognized contact allergen.

name: iodopropynyl butylcarbamate
note: Preservative; emerging contact allergen.

name: benzophenone-3
note: Chemical UV filter (oxybenzone); a leading cause of sunscreen-related contact and photoallergic reactions.

name: butyl methoxydibenzoylmethane
note: Chemical UV filter (avobenzone); can cause contact and photoallergic reactions.

name: octocrylene
note: Chemical UV filter; documented contact and photoallergen, may cross-react with ketoprofen.

name: ethylhexyl methoxycinnamate
note: Chemical UV filter (octinoxate); can cause contact and photoallergic reactions.

name: homosalate
note: Chemical UV filter; occasional contact allergen.

name: ethylhexyl salicylate
note: Chemical UV filter (octisalate); occasional contact allergen.

name: paba
note: Older chemical UV filter; classic photoallergen, largely phased out.

name: lanolin
note: Wool-derived emollient; a common allergen in people with atopic dermatitis.

name: propylene glycol
note: Humectant and solvent; both an irritant and occasional allergen, especially on compromised skin barriers.

name: cocamidopropyl betaine
note: Surfactant in cleansers and shampoos; well-documented contact allergen.

name: sodium lauryl sulfate
note: Strong surfactant; an irritant (not allergen) that can disrupt an already-fragile skin barrier.

name: alcohol denat
note: Drying solvent; can irritate and dehydrate compromised skin.

name: melaleuca alternifolia leaf oil
note: Tea tree oil; oxidized tea tree oil is a recognized contact allergen.
